headline: Seasonal Wildlife and State Park Excursions
reservation: Guided eagle tours and park-managed cabins require advance booking through the Tennessee State Parks system. While lake entry is open, specific boat permits and hunting season schedules must be verified through the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency as policies vary annually.

days.title: Flooded Forests and Earthquakes

stops.name: Reelfoot Lake State Park Visitor Center
stops.detail: Learn about the 1811-1812 New Madrid earthquakes and the unique 'stump jumper' boats.

stops.name: Cypress Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk over the wetlands to observe the distinctive cypress knees and local waterfowl.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; local roads are flat and easily navigable.
days.note: Pack high-quality insect repellent for any boardwalk explorations during warmer months.

days.title: Coves, Basins, and Eagles

stops.name: Blue Basin
stops.detail: Take a guided boat tour to navigate the submerged stumps and lotus beds.

stops.name: Airpark Area
stops.detail: Explore the northern reaches of the lake for bird watching and quieter shoreline views.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; transit between eastern and western shores varies by road condition.
days.note: Winter visitors should dress in multiple heavy layers for open-air eagle tours.

days.title: Heritage and Regional Wildlife

stops.name: Reelfoot National Wildlife Refuge
stops.detail: Observe migratory birds and local reptiles in a protected conservation environment.

stops.name: Keiser Lake Road
stops.detail: Drive the perimeter for agricultural views and additional wildlife spotting opportunities.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; gravel sections may be soft after heavy Tennessee rains.
days.note: Check the Wildlife Management Area schedule as certain zones close for hunting seasons.

intel.title: Public Ramps
intel.text: Parking at main boat ramps in Samburg can be competitive during the spring fishing rush. Utilize park-designated lots to avoid blocking narrow levee roads.

intel.title: Rural Connectivity
intel.text: Signal strength is generally stable in Tiptonville but drops significantly on the water or in the Wildlife Refuge. Carry a printed map for navigating the backroads of the lake's north end.

intel.title: Tiptonville Hub
intel.text: Tiptonville is the primary source for fuel and supplies in this remote corner of Tennessee. Ensure you have adequate provisions before heading to the eastern shoreline or refuge trails.

intel.title: Fishing and Eagles
intel.text: January and February are peak for eagles, while April dominates the fishing calendar. Aim for mid-week visits to avoid the highest concentration of local anglers.

intel.title: Water Navigation
intel.text: The lake is filled with submerged timber; only shallow-draft boats are recommended. Visitors unfamiliar with the 'stumps' should use local guides to avoid hull damage.

plan.arrival: Fly into MKL and drive approximately two hours northwest, stopping in Union City for groceries and local information.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is fine for town and park roads, though high clearance helps on refuge tracks.
plan.goldenHour: Reelfoot Lake Shoreline provides silhouettes of cypress trees at dusk; winter colors are particularly stark.
